problem: addToDate() in tools/tools.js uses setMonth, so Jan 31 + 1 month returns Mar 3 (verified in node) and Mar 31 minus 1 month returns Mar 3; add-subtract page says "adding 1 month to January 31st gives February 28th ... not March 3rd".
fix: In addToDate, after adding years/months, clamp the day to the last day of the target month (new Date(y, m+1, 0).getDate()); then apply weeks/days. Also Feb 29 minus/plus years should land on Feb 28. No page text changes, the existing sentence becomes true.
translation_detail: Script change only (tools/tools.js). add-subtract is live in ja; text already says the correct behaviour.

problem: ymdBetween() clamps negative days to 0: Jan 31 to Mar 1 gives 1 month 0 days, but age-calculator text says "1 month and 1 day"; born Jan 29-31 users lose days around end of February.
fix: Compute months by adding whole months to the start with end-of-month clamping (Jan 31 + 1 month = Feb 28), then count the remaining days to the end date. Alternatively change the example sentence, but fixing the code keeps the text.
translation_detail: Script only. age-calculator is live in ja (text unchanged); days-until-birthday is live in ja.

problem: Page says if Jan 1 is Fri/Sat/Sun "week 1 of the new ISO year starts on the Monday before New Year's Day". It starts on the Monday after (2027: Jan 4; Jan 1 2027 is ISO week 53 of 2026, verified).
fix: Replace the paragraph with: "If January 1 falls on a Friday, Saturday or Sunday, it belongs to the last week of the previous ISO year, and week 1 starts on the first Monday after it (January 2 to 4). If January 1 falls on a Monday to Thursday, week 1 is the week that contains it, which can start in late December."
translation_detail: unit td70d897ae4 in i18n/tools/en.json; iso-week-number is not live in any locale (ja 0%).

problem: Due date = LMP + 280*86400000 ms: for LMPs from roughly mid-April to early June in DST-observing zones the date shown is one day early (LMP 2027-04-20 in New York/London shows Jan 24, correct Jan 25). The trimester line says "Week 9, Day 1" while the stat above says 8 weeks pregnant.
fix: Use setDate(getDate()+280) for the due date. Show gestational age consistently as "8 weeks 1 day" in both places (change the pregWeekDay string).
translation_detail: runtime string result.pregWeekDay in i18n/tools-runtime/en.json; page not live in any locale.

problem: Medical topic with no disclaimer, no source and no cycle-length or conception/IVF option; the 4% and 38-42 week claims are uncited. NHS and Tommy's calculators offer cycle length and link to a midwife.
fix: Add: "This is an estimate. Your midwife or doctor will confirm your due date, usually from a dating scan around 12 weeks." and cite the NHS due-date calculator and Tommy's (only about 4 in 100 babies arrive on the due date). Add a cycle-length field (adjust LMP by cycle minus 28 days).
translation_detail: Changed t597d82a11d; new disclaimer, source line, field label. Not live in any locale.

problem: yearsLeft = min(105, baseline+adjustments) - age, with baselines 73.8 (M) and 79.0 (F): with neutral answers a 70-year-old man gets about 4 years left, where actuarial tables give well over 10 (SSA period life table); adjustments are additive, unsourced, and the lede says "research-based" while the body says "simplified assumption, not an official statistic"; meta desc says "population baselines and research-adjusted factors".
fix: Base years left on remaining life expectancy at the current age from a published table (SSA period life table or ONS/WHO) and apply the adjustments to that; cite the table and the sources for each adjustment (e.g. smoking, exercise meta-analyses). Reword the lede to "A rough estimate of your life expectancy from simple lifestyle adjustments" and the meta to "Estimate your remaining years from your age, sex and lifestyle. A rough, educational estimate based on life-table averages, not medical advice."
translation_detail: lede t69ba522453, cap paragraph t172ddacbaa, desc af17ed8cdd5 + JSON-LD lf17ed8cdd5, plus new source line(s). Live in ja (88 units): ja stays above 90% but the changed units fall back to English until retranslated.

problem: End-of-fasting lists "16-24 hours: ketosis beginning, autophagy increasing; 24-72 hours: significant autophagy" with no source (search found only generic wellness timelines; human autophagy timing is not established); intermittent page calls 36-hour fasts "e.g., 5:2 protocol" (5:2 is two low-calorie days, not 36 h fasts) and says OMAD is "effective for weight loss"; none has a medical caveat except one clause.
fix: Replace the stage list with "What people commonly describe" wording without autophagy figures, or drop it; fix 5:2 ("5:2 means eating normally five days and about 500-600 kcal on two"); cut "effective for weight loss" or cite a review; add a caveat on all three: "Not suitable if you are pregnant, under 18, have diabetes or a history of eating disorders, or take medication; talk to a doctor first." Link an NHS/Mayo Clinic page.
translation_detail: End-of-fasting t50af1fdaad, t91e8d57190, tecf3380abd; intermittent t405bb3ebd7, t4e3ba8def8; plus 3 caveat sentences. None live in ja.

problem: Index card text describes features the tools lack: pregnancy "From last menstrual period, conception date, or ultrasound" (LMP only), sleep "Calculate how long you will sleep between bedtime and alarm" (it suggests bed/wake times), fasting duration "Hours and minutes between two fast times" (it takes last-meal time and protocol).
fix: Pregnancy: "Estimated due date and current week from your last period." Sleep: "Best bedtimes and wake-up times from 90-minute sleep cycles." Fasting: "When your 16:8, 18:6 or custom fast ends from the time you last ate."
translation_detail: index units t686d87a9e2, t380c07f32f, tc3168bd642; /tools/ is live in ja (203 units), those 3 fall back to English until retranslated (stays above 90%).

problem: 90-minute cycles and "wake at the end of a cycle and feel refreshed" are stated as fact; cycle length varies between people and nights; 7.5 h called "ideal" while the cited National Sleep Foundation range is 7-9 h; no link.
fix: Say "average cycle of about 90 minutes; yours may be 70-120", link the Sleep Foundation or AASM/SRS recommendation (7 or more hours for adults), and relabel 7.5 h as "a common target" rather than ideal. Add a line: "If you regularly feel unrested, see a doctor."
translation_detail: tc9f5b1d091, t5522bc12dc, meta a88db384279 + l88db384279 (if desc reworded). Not live in any locale.

problem: No tool page shows a published/updated date, author or reviewer, and JSON-LD has no dateModified/author; the "next five years" tables (Easter 2027-31, equinoxes, weekday tables, 2027 business-day table) are hard-coded and go stale each year.

Add a one-line "How we check" note on pages with calculations.
